title: Pre-Analysis — Light-Emitting Diode Floor Proximity Marking, Revision B Scope
abstract: Closed pre-analysis run against the released light-emitting diode floor marking change ahead of its Revision B, which extended the standard to the remaining photoluminescent fleet and added the premium cabin layouts.

sections.objective: Before Revision B extended the light-emitting diode marking standard to the aircraft still carrying the photoluminescent strip, establish what the wider effectivity would break. Three questions were put: whether the earlier standard can be withdrawn cleanly, whether the bulletin that installs the photoluminescent strip has to be closed first, and what the extension costs in cabin floor access on aircraft with a premium layout in the forward cabin.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed, one blocking. The photoluminescent standard is not simply older, it is the certified means of compliance on the aircraft that carry it, and withdrawing it before every one of those aircraft has taken the diode standard would leave a gap in the emergency lighting compliance statement. That made the withdrawal sequence, not the design, the pacing item. The bulletin that installs the strip is still open on eleven aircraft and had to be closed in a controlled order. The parts figure carries both marking families under one item group and needed splitting. The last item is quieter but real: the seat track work in the same floor region lifts the panels the marking is bonded to, so an operator taking both in one visit saves a full cabin-out.
sections.next_steps: Publish the withdrawal sequence for the photoluminescent standard tied to diode embodiment per aircraft, not per fleet. Close the strip installation bulletin in a controlled order and notify the eleven affected operators. Split the marking families in the parts content and give each its own effectivity rather than relying on a note. Offer the combined embodiment with the seat track work to operators who have embodied neither, with the marking length per aircraft costed as a consumable. Confirm with continued airworthiness that the per-aircraft withdrawal sequence is acceptable before the revision is issued.

tasks.title: Traverse the marking standard supersession chain on ATA 33-20-13
Establish the compliance position during the transition
Identify cabin floor work sharing the same access

expected_findings.rationale: The photoluminescent standard is the certified means of compliance on the aircraft that carry it. Withdrawing it on a fleet date rather than per aircraft would leave a compliance gap on every aircraft that had not yet taken the diode standard.
expected_findings.resolution: Tie the withdrawal to per-aircraft diode embodiment and publish the sequence with the revision.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin installing the photoluminescent strip is still open on eleven aircraft. Extending the diode standard over the same population without closing it leaves two live bulletins offering different compliance routes for the same requirement.
expected_findings.resolution: Close the strip bulletin in a controlled order and notify the affected operators before the revision is released.

expected_findings.rationale: Both marking families sit in one item group with a shared attachment set. The wider effectivity makes the mixed fleet last longer, so the figure has to distinguish them properly rather than rely on a note.
expected_findings.resolution: Split the item group by marking family and give each its own effectivity.

evidence.similarity_note: Retrieved through the shared cabin equipment chapter and by similarity on floor panel lifting and cabin-out downtime language.

expected_findings.rationale: The seat track splice work lifts the same floor panels the marking is bonded to, and the marking has to be replaced on any panel joint disturbed. Operators taking both in one visit avoid paying for the marking twice.
expected_findings.resolution: Offer a combined embodiment package to operators with neither change embodied.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the ATA 25-20 cabin chapter and reads as forward cabin floor work, but it replaces seat track splice hardware under the floor and has no lighting or marking content, no shared part number, no shared functional item and no zone overlap with the marking run.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. The compliance transition sequence was the pacing item and was published with Revision B. The bulletin closure and the parts split followed in the same package.
